paragraphs.title: A Request for Protection and Guidance

easy.explanation: He says, “In thee, O LORD, do I put my trust.”
easy.q: In whom does the speaker put his trust?

easy.explanation: He asks, “deliver me in thy righteousness.”
easy.q: What does the speaker ask the LORD to do?

easy.explanation: He says, “Into thine hand I commit my spirit.”
easy.q: Into whose hand does the speaker commit his spirit?

answers: So he can find his enemies
So he can leave his family
medium.explanation: He says, “for thy name’s sake lead me, and guide me.”
medium.q: Why does the speaker ask the LORD to lead and guide him?

answers: A place of strength and safety
medium.explanation: The speaker calls the LORD his rock, fortress, and strength.
medium.q: What does “strong rock” suggest about the LORD?

answers: The net secretly laid for him
medium.explanation: He asks, “Pull me out of the net that they have laid privily for me.”
medium.q: What trap does the speaker ask to escape?

answers: Trust, deliverance, guidance, and escape from a trap
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from trusting the LORD to asking for rescue, guidance, and escape.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly summarizes the speaker’s requests?

answers: He is a source of stability and protection
He is a source of amusement
challenge.explanation: These images portray safety, strength, and refuge.
challenge.q: What do “rock” and “fortress” communicate about God?

answers: He trusts the LORD as the God of truth
challenge.explanation: He commits himself to the LORD, whom he calls “O LORD God of truth.”
challenge.q: Why can the speaker entrust his spirit to the LORD?

paragraphs.title: Trust in God and Joy in His Kindness

easy.explanation: He says, “I have hated them that regard lying vanities.”
easy.q: What does the speaker hate?

easy.explanation: He says, “I trust in the LORD.”
easy.q: In whom does the speaker trust?

easy.explanation: He says, “I will be glad and rejoice in thy mercy.”
easy.q: In what does the speaker rejoice?

answers: Only the plans of his enemies
medium.explanation: The speaker says, “thou hast considered my trouble.”
medium.q: What has the LORD considered?

answers: The LORD brought him into freedom and safety
The LORD caused him to become lost
medium.explanation: A large room contrasts with confinement and suggests relief and freedom.
medium.q: What does setting the speaker’s feet in “a large room” suggest?

answers: The LORD has seen his trouble and known his soul
medium.explanation: The LORD has considered his trouble and known him in adversity.
medium.q: Why does the speaker rejoice in the LORD’s mercy?

answers: Lying vanities versus trust in the LORD
challenge.explanation: The speaker rejects worthless vanities and chooses to trust the LORD.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast in this passage?

answers: A movement from distress to relief
A movement from joy to sorrow
A movement from faith to despair
challenge.explanation: The large room pictures deliverance from confinement and trouble.
challenge.q: What does the movement into a “large room” represent?

answers: Rejecting vanities, trusting, rejoicing, and recognizing mercy
challenge.explanation: The speaker rejects false things, trusts God, and rejoices in His mercy.
challenge.q: Which emotional sequence best fits these verses?

easy.explanation: He says, “I am in trouble.”
easy.q: What condition does the speaker describe?

answers: It has disappeared from his enemies
easy.explanation: He says, “my strength faileth because of mine iniquity.”
easy.q: What has happened to his strength?

easy.explanation: He describes himself as a reproach and a fear to others.
easy.q: How does the speaker describe his standing among people?

answers: His eyes and body are weakened by sorrow
His eyes are filled with happiness
medium.explanation: The phrase describes physical weakness caused by intense grief.
medium.q: What does “mine eye is consumed with grief” mean in context?

answers: Slander, enemies, and fear on every side
medium.explanation: He heard the slander of many and says, “fear was on every side.”
medium.q: What made the speaker feel threatened?

answers: He is forgotten as a dead man and compared to a broken vessel
medium.explanation: He says, “I am forgotten as a dead man out of mind: I am like a broken vessel.”
medium.q: Why is the speaker’s sense of loneliness especially strong?

answers: Grief and sighing weaken the whole person
challenge.explanation: Grief, sighing, failing strength, and consumed bones are all joined together.
challenge.q: What connection does the passage make between bodily weakness and inner distress?

answers: It shows harm to the speaker’s reputation as well as danger
challenge.explanation: Slander attacks his name while enemies plot against his life.
challenge.q: What does the slander of many add to the description of persecution?

challenge.explanation: He says, “I am like a broken vessel,” emphasizing rejection and worthlessness.
challenge.q: Which image most strongly expresses the speaker’s feeling of being forgotten?

easy.explanation: He says, “I said, Thou art my God.”
easy.q: What does the speaker declare about the LORD?

easy.explanation: He says, “My times are in thy hand.”
easy.q: In whose hand are the speaker’s times?

easy.explanation: He asks, “deliver me from the hand of mine enemies.”
easy.q: What does the speaker ask the LORD to do?

medium.explanation: He asks to be delivered from his enemies and from those who persecute him.
medium.q: From whom does the speaker ask to be delivered?

answers: A request for favor, mercy, and salvation
A request for God to hide
medium.explanation: The request is connected with being saved for God’s mercies’ sake.
medium.q: What does “Make thy face to shine upon thy servant” express?

medium.explanation: He asks, “Let the lying lips be put to silence.”
medium.q: What does the speaker want to happen to lying lips?

answers: He trusts the LORD and commits his times to Him
He asks his enemies for help
challenge.explanation: Even under threat, he says, “I trusted in thee, O LORD.”
challenge.q: How does the speaker respond to persecution?

answers: The speaker calls upon God, while the wicked speak lies
Both trust in the same thing
The speaker lies while the wicked pray
challenge.explanation: The speaker seeks God’s mercy, while the wicked are described by lying lips.
challenge.q: What contrast appears between the speaker and the wicked?

answers: Slander and proud speech are part of the danger from which he seeks rescue
Lies are the source of his joy
Silence is meant to hide God’s mercy
challenge.explanation: The speaker seeks protection from both physical enemies and harmful accusations.
challenge.q: Why is the request for lying lips to be silenced connected with salvation?

paragraphs.title: God’s Goodness and Protection of His Beloved

easy.explanation: He exclaims, “Oh how great is thy goodness.”
easy.q: What does the speaker praise as great?

easy.explanation: The goodness is laid up “for them that fear thee.”
easy.q: For whom has the LORD laid up His goodness?

easy.explanation: The LORD keeps them from “the strife of tongues.”
easy.q: From what does the LORD protect His people?

answers: In the secret of His presence and in a pavilion
In the houses of their enemies
medium.explanation: He hides them in the secret of His presence and keeps them in a pavilion.
medium.q: Where does the LORD hide His people?

medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the proud threats and opposition of people.
medium.q: What does “the pride of man” represent in this passage?

answers: His goodness is shown by sheltering those who trust Him
His goodness is reserved only for the wicked
medium.explanation: God’s goodness is expressed through hiding and protecting His people.
medium.q: What is the connection between God’s goodness and His protection?

answers: It is laid up for those who fear God and shown before people
It is hidden from everyone and does not exist
It is given only to persecutors
challenge.explanation: The goodness is stored for God’s people and worked openly before others.
challenge.q: What contrast appears in the description of God’s goodness?

challenge.explanation: A pavilion represents a protected place where God keeps His people.
challenge.q: What does the image of a “pavilion” communicate?

answers: Great goodness, trust, shelter, and protection from hostile speech
challenge.explanation: The passage praises God’s goodness and describes His protection from human hostility.
challenge.q: Which sequence best summarizes these verses?

easy.explanation: He says the LORD “hath shewed me his marvellous kindness.”
easy.q: For what does the speaker bless the LORD?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “in a strong city.”
easy.q: Where did the LORD show this kindness?

easy.explanation: He says, “thou heardest the voice of my supplications.”
easy.q: What did the speaker learn after crying to the LORD?

answers: That he was cut off from before the LORD’s eyes
That he was in a large room
medium.explanation: He says, “I am cut off from before thine eyes.”
medium.q: What did the speaker think in his haste?

answers: In a moment of panic or distress
medium.explanation: The phrase describes the speaker’s hurried and fearful thought.
medium.q: What does “in my haste” mean here?

answers: He moves from thinking God had abandoned him to knowing God heard him
He moves from faith to despair
He moves from joy to fear
medium.explanation: Although he feared being cut off, he later affirms that God heard his prayer.
medium.q: What change occurs between the speaker’s fear and his later testimony?

answers: Distress can produce mistaken thoughts, but prayer restores trust
Distress always gives a perfectly accurate view
Distress removes the need for prayer
challenge.explanation: The speaker admits a fearful thought but then testifies that God heard him.
challenge.q: What does this passage teach about feelings during distress?

answers: The speaker recognizes God’s kindness after deliverance
challenge.explanation: His thanksgiving comes from discovering that God heard his supplications.
challenge.q: Why does thanksgiving follow the description of fear?

answers: Even in danger and confinement, the LORD can hear and show kindness
challenge.explanation: God showed kindness and heard the speaker even in a place of danger.
challenge.q: How are a strong city and answered prayer connected?

paragraphs.title: Encouragement for Those Who Hope in God

easy.explanation: He says, “O love the LORD, all ye his saints.”
easy.q: To whom does the speaker give his final command?

easy.explanation: He says, “Be of good courage.”
easy.q: What does he tell those who hope in the LORD to do?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “the LORD preserveth the faithful.”
easy.q: Whom does the LORD preserve?

answers: Love and trust in the LORD give His people strength
medium.explanation: The call to love the LORD is followed by the call to be courageous.
medium.q: What connection does the passage make between loving the LORD and courage?

answers: The LORD will give inner strength
The LORD will break the heart
The LORD will hide the heart
medium.explanation: The phrase promises courage and inward strength from the LORD.
medium.q: What does “he shall strengthen your heart” mean?

answers: The LORD preserves the faithful and strengthens them
They will be delivered to persecutors
medium.explanation: The closing verse promises preservation and strengthened hearts.
medium.q: What encouragement is given to those who hope in the LORD?

answers: He encourages others because he has learned that the LORD hears and preserves
He ignores what happened to him
He warns people not to trust the LORD
challenge.explanation: After experiencing distress and deliverance, he calls others to courage and hope.
challenge.q: How does the ending relate to the speaker’s personal experience?

answers: Faithfulness to the LORD brings courage, preservation, and hope
Persecution is the path to safety
Lying is the source of salvation
challenge.explanation: The conclusion emphasizes loving the LORD, trusting Him, and receiving strength.
challenge.q: Which principle best summarizes the final verses?

answers: The personal testimony becomes encouragement for all God’s faithful people
The speaker begins talking only about enemies
challenge.explanation: The speaker moves from his own experience to a command addressed to all the saints.
challenge.q: What is the effect of the shift from “I” to “ye”?
